purpose: Classify the completed full-expansion proof rows before changing product routing. Classification is advisory for productization only; it does not itself promote support.

productCandidateContract.note: A product-candidate classification does not route product traffic by itself. Product routing may accept only rows that also satisfy this contract at implementation time.

rows.reason: Exact target-native two-process pipe support is proven, but it has no productPath marker yet and must not be exposed as broad process-graph movement.
Finite captured pipe bytes are target-native replayed and already serve as support evidence for generic-stdio-pipe-product-marker; product use is allowed only through exact productPath metadata.
nonClaims: no live kernel pipe queue migration beyond explicit captured bytes

rows.reason: This row is the fail-closed sibling for unsafe pipe/stdio states and is required evidence for pipe product candidates.
This row carries exact live-capture productPath metadata, refusalClasses=[], support proof generic-finite-pipe-buffer-replay, refusal proof generic-pipe-stdio-refusals, and target output evidence.
This row records fail-closed boundaries for unsafe multi-process pipe shapes and must remain a guard, not a support claim.
This row refuses service-managed children, dynamic pools, active requests, reload races, and non-exact trees; it is boundary evidence only.
The safe exact prefork daemon row is proven with a proof-only Python fixture and health probe; it is not product support until a real product marker and package boundary are proven.
This row is the fail-closed service-process-tree boundary for dynamic workers, active requests, reload races, config drift, writable persistence, and package/config mismatch.
The exact pathname listener/client-pair shape is target-native and promising, but product routing needs productPath metadata and a product-facing marker before promotion.
This row refuses connected sessions, abstract sockets, datagrams, socketpairs, fd passing, credential-sensitive sockets, and unsafe pathname state.
The target-native relative one-shot timerfd primitive is proven, but product support needs an enclosing exact process/resource envelope and productPath marker.
This row refuses realtime, nonblocking, unread, absolute, and periodic timerfd shapes and must remain guard evidence.
Signal state is refusal-only in the full expansion: signalfd, pending signals, process-group ambiguity, runtime signal timers, and unknown handlers fail before target launch.
A single whole-file exclusive advisory flock can be reacquired target-side, but product support needs an enclosing command/resource envelope and marker.
This row refuses lock conflicts, unknown owners, mandatory locks, leases, nonseekable offsets, changed backing files, unsupported lock types, and cross-process ownership ambiguity.
nonClaims: no mandatory lock or lease support

neededBeforePromotion: clear no queued event replay explanation

rows.reason: This row refuses queued watcher events, recursive watches, fanotify permission events, unsupported masks, and active waiters.
Clean file-backed mmap identity reconstruction is proven as a primitive, but product routing needs an enclosing exact product envelope and dirty-map refusal pairing.
This row refuses dirty, anonymous, private/shared ambiguous, changed backing, writable executable, and runtime heap mmap shapes.
A one-level epoll timerfd readiness primitive is proven, but product support needs an enclosing exact product envelope and productPath marker.
This row refuses unsupported epoll flags, aliases, nested epoll, unknown fds, active wait loops, and unsupported readiness sources.

The exact idle Redis parity row is support evidence for redis-live-generic-primary-marker, but product use must remain limited to the exact empty/idle supported shape and never become broad database migration.

rows.reason: This row refuses metadata-only success, source-ISA emulation, runtime-profile shortcuts, arbitrary ELF/process claims, unsupported resources, missing tools, and incomplete graphs.
